patch.value:
## Outcome
The pm SDK is a complete, documented, public API for repository-native project context. The CLI is one presentation layer over it; MCP is another; third parties can build a third.

## Why this is a milestone, not an epic
pm-usfg is the living promotion epic. This milestone is the outcome gate that the universal-domain milestone and the GA semver surface both consume.

## Delivery chain
Remaining pm-usfg promotion slices -> boundary ratchet hardened to a failing gate -> authoring docs and exemplar -> pm-feecbs conformance gate can then measure external packages against a stable surface.

## Explicit non-goals
Not an API freeze — semver commitments belong to the GA milestone. Not a rewrite: promotion moves code, it does not redesign it.
Outcome milestone: SDK-complete core — every CLI and MCP capability reachable from the public pm SDK

SDK import-boundary baseline is zero and the ratchet is a hard failing gate, not an allowlist; Every remaining promotion slice under pm-usfg is closed with public exports and authoring docs; A published exemplar package implements a complete workflow using only public SDK exports, with no local shim; CLI and MCP handlers contain argument parsing, rendering, and no domain logic, proven by a structural test
The CLI and MCP server contain presentation logic only; every primitive they use is public SDK surface
The SDK is the product's leverage point: anything not in it cannot be reused, embedded, or extended by third parties.
Unblocks the universal-platform milestone, the conformance gate for external packages, and any embedding of pm in another runtime.
The private-core import baseline is zero and hard-gated; a non-trivial third-party surface is buildable against published SDK exports alone.
Every new command shipped against private core widens the promotion backlog; the boundary ratchet only holds if the remaining slices land.

value.text:
Independent external-consumer verification, 2026-08-03, against the published 2026.8.3 tarball rather than the working tree.

Method: install @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.8.3 into a clean throwaway npm project with no repository access, import only the entrypoints the package exports map declares, and check whether the symbols our own CLI depends on are actually reachable from there. This is the outside view of the milestone's claim - it cannot be satisfied by anything in src/.

Result, and it is a good one. Of the 30 distinct SDK symbols src/cli imports, 29 resolve from the public entrypoints; the single apparent miss is an artifact of my extraction reading 'runValidate as runSdkValidate' as one name. So the capability half of this milestone holds under external observation: a third party importing only @unbrained/pm-cli/sdk and its declared subpaths can reach what our own command layer runs on.

One thing this measurement is NOT evidence for, stated so it is not over-read later. src/cli imports through 79 distinct deep module paths (sdk/runtime-primitives.js with 19 uses, sdk/files.js, sdk/query/list.js, sdk/telemetry.js and so on), and the exports map declares 10 subpaths. The deep paths are genuinely unreachable externally - probing four of them from the installed package returns ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. That is path hygiene, not a capability gap, because every symbol behind those paths is re-exported through a public barrel. I initially read the 79-versus-10 ratio as a falsification of this milestone and it is not; recording the correction here so the ratio is not cited as a gap.

The property that keeps this true is already owned and already gated: pm-xpumg4 closed having delivered a fail-closed shrinking ratchet that computes transitive public exports and rejects new private imports, and it passes in the current tree. The residual risk it manages is the seven grandfathered entries its close note reports, not the import-path count.

Net: the SDK-complete claim is externally verified at the symbol level as of 2026.8.3. What remains unmeasured by this probe is whether every CLI *capability* - as opposed to every symbol the CLI happens to import - has a public SDK expression, which is a different question and the one the milestone still has to answer.
